title: One captured transition
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $D$ be a four-work-tape machine over the Boolean alphabet with finite state set and decidable state equality, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$. If $c$ is not halted, one step of the capture wrapper from the first-phase configuration associated to $c$ equals the first-phase configuration associated to the result of one step of $M$ from $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state machine over the Boolean alphabet
$D$ is a four-work-tape Boolean machine with finite state set and decidable state equality
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on the finite Boolean input $x$
replaced:
Let $c$ be a configuration of a machine $M$ on input $x$ whose control state
is live (not halted).  Then one transition of the output-capture wrapper of
$M$ and a four-tape interpreter $D$, applied to the first-phase embedding of
$c$, equals the first-phase embedding of the configuration obtained from $c$
by one transition of $M$.  In particular any bit emitted by that transition
of $M$ --- including a bit emitted on $M$'s halting transition --- is
appended on the table tape, and the wrapper itself remains live.
